message.content: In computer‑vision contexts, “purple” is usually just another hue in the RGB or HSV color space that can be used for labeling, segmentation, or visual distinction. It’s not a special semantic class on its own—rather, it’s one of many colors that can be assigned to a particular object or region in an image to help humans or algorithms differentiate it from other parts. For example, in a semantic‑segmentation mask, a purple pixel might indicate a specific class (e.g., “road sign”) while other colors indicate other classes. Purple can also be used as a placeholder or highlight color in UI overlays, heat maps, or debugging visualizations.
